scope: What the first external testers and 1.0.0.13's first session asked for: the headset PC folds each controller's acceleration into the poses it sends, so the rendering PC's first-order prediction lands where a swinging hand will be; the rendering PC renders at the headset PC's recommended size (at most 1.5 x the stream) and scales down for the encoder; Auto codec is HEVC on every headset, 10-bit where the headset PC decodes it, the Bazzite client reading the GPU's VA-API decoder profiles; the automatic bitrate's ceiling is 0.30 bit per pixel for HEVC (0.42 H.264, 0.25 AV1); on Bazzite a headset PC on its network by cable and Wi-Fi is offered two standard settings once, which keep the video on the cable with Wi-Fi connected, and a Wi-Fi pause that cuts the host off is undone at once; paired headset PCs start sessions on any Windows network type, the firewall rules admitting only the local subnet; the gaze is predicted through the head's turn; the host keeps its last session's statistics for a report made after a restart. Every package carries version 1.0.0.14; the clients' native client is rebuilt, the runtime probe relabelled, and the host's driver is 1.0.0.9's.

from_the_session.what: 1.0.0.13, an hour of Beat Saber at Native with Medium foveation, HEVC 10-bit, wired, on a handheld headset PC on Bazzite; the host report the maintainer sent (its own side empty after a restart of the host's VROSTBridge, the headset PC's report carried inside); and the first external testers' feedback.
went_well: the stream chosen before the session and the wired parity (490 frames rebuilt, 35 lost in an hour)
about 31 ms through the pipeline; the testers found the latency good and the foveation invisible
the menu button opens the rendering PC's SteamVR menu (a tester quit the game from it)
put_right: testing this build: with the other Wi-Fi paused every Start failed (Network is unreachable: the cable had no route to the host once Wi-Fi was gone); with the pause off the video arrived on the Wi-Fi card (7.5 million packets against 77 thousand on the cable) and Wi-Fi's background scan stalled the picture every ~300 s
testing this build: the rendering PC refused sessions until Windows' network was set back to Private

the first build's receive-buffer fix was misjudged: it read rmem_default as the limit, while the stream's socket gets twice rmem_max (8 MiB on Bazzite); 1.0.0.13's RcvbufErrors count every UDP socket on the PC
the testers missed notes they had swung at: the host's first-order prediction lands a h^2/2 short of an accelerating hand, and the client's own check measured maxima of 170 to 280 mm per ten seconds

fine detail softer than on a directly connected headset: the host rendered at the stream size, Auto codec was H.264 on an Index, and the 0.22 bit per pixel ceiling held the session to 65 Mbit/s while the link had room
the sharp region landed behind the gaze during head turns, the gaze being 30 to 40 ms old at the host
the host report arrived empty because the host's companion had been restarted
from_the_session.not_put_right: a change of direction within the latency, which neither PC can predict; the 17 ms of the pipeline spent waiting for the display (the headset PC's SteamVR as a second compositor); the rendering PC's stalls; whether the remembered GPU clock was held from the start (800 MHz for the first 50 s: the next session's held_from_start decides).
from_the_session.asked_for: by the maintainer: improve it the best you can; nothing pushed or published until it is tested.

changes: client/device/acceleration.hpp (new), openvr_device.cpp/.hpp, prediction_check.hpp, main.cpp: each controller's acceleration estimated from consecutive samples (EMA 12 ms, bounded 60 m/s^2 and 400 rad/s^2, reset after a gap) and folded into the sent pose and velocity (p - a h^2/2, v + a h; the orientation and angular velocity likewise), so the host's extrapolation by h is second order with no change on the wire; the prediction check measures the host's result from the sent values against the measured pose; --no-acceleration (settings prediction_acceleration); TIMING acceleration_samples and acceleration_max

client/device/gaze_prediction.hpp (new), gaze.hpp, openvr_device.cpp: the gaze turned by the head's angular velocity in the head's frame over the sample's age plus the host's step, bounded at 0.35 rad, before it is sent; TIMING gaze_predicted and gaze_turn_max_deg

client/platform/linux/vaapi_profiles.hpp (new), vulkan.cpp, CMakeLists.txt (libva, libva-drm): the GPU's VA-API decoder profiles (H.264, HEVC, HEVC Main10, AV1, 10-bit AV1) reported in a STATUS line; launcher/app.py remembers them (decoder_profiles, logged as DECODERS)
launcher/headset.py: automatic_codec: Auto is HEVC unless the decoder profiles say no HEVC and H.264 present; the resolution options and the stream preferences use it

host/profile.py: render_width: ALVR's emulated headset width is the headset PC's recommended width, at most 1.5 x the stream width, aligned to 32; the transcoding width stays the stream's; the host log names both

launcher/network_settings.py (new), app.py, desktop.html, game_ui.py: a headset PC on its subnet more than once (shared_network) without arp_ignore/arp_announce, or a receive buffer that gives the stream under 4 MiB, is said in the log (NETWORK) and on the page; fix-network installs /etc/sysctl.d/70-vrostbridge-network.conf (arp_ignore 1, arp_announce 2, rmem_max and rmem_default 16 MiB) through pkexec install and pkexec sysctl -p, no shell; the status and the report carry network_settings

launcher/wifi_others.py, app.py: a wired stream leaves Wi-Fi connected when the system keeps the stream on the cable (the settings above; always on Windows); otherwise a pause is followed by a pinned connection to the host's session port, and on failure the kernel's route is logged and the pause undone (resume_now); adapter_counters.elsewhere and check_video_path log VIDEO_PATH once when the video arrives on another adapter

host/control.py, app.py, session_link.py, host/Host-Setup.ps1, launcher/Client-Firewall.ps1, client_network.py: require_home_network needs a connected network, not a Private one; pairing_network_private keeps Private (or domain) for a new client's automatic pairing only; both firewall scripts create their rules with -Profile Any -RemoteAddress LocalSubnet (the check expects Any, so an upgrade updates them with one prompt)

launcher/adapter_counters.py: linux_udp_sockets: the stream (9944) and gaze (9005) sockets' own drops from /proc/net/udp, in adapter_counters.sockets; launcher/gaze_provider.py: the relay socket asks for 4 MiB

launcher/last_session.py (new), app.py: host-last-session.json written every minute while streaming and at Stop (event statistics, pipeline summary, adapter counters, the driver's VROST_* lines without tracking data; cut to the statistics above 2 MB); a host report made with no session since the companion started carries it as host_last_session
